workarounds.note: each plate style sets minHeight to the page's 210 mm, because a design's images reserve no height: without it the storm's right half, which draws no text, keeps only its heading's own 7.6 mm line and the next text starts on that page (gotcha opener-image-no-reserve)

the plate styles set zero margins, so the column is as tall as minHeight: in the text pages' 158 mm column, 1.4.1 drops a 210 mm reservation whole and the three texts print over the plates before them (gotcha opener-taller-than-column)

level 1 states breakBefore { enabled: false }, which changes nothing in 1.4.1 (it already drops the H1 break once a headings object exists); when the default always-odd break comes back, the setting stops the texts from breaking, so their pages stay body pages with a folio (gotcha headings-drop-h1-break)
col() writes the hex beside each paletteId, because 1.4.1 paints design elements (the captions, the cover title, the folio) and bodyText.referenceColor from the hex (gotcha palette-skips-designs)

design text lineHeight is a multiple of the size (1 for the cover title, 1.05 for the text titles, 1.5 for the colophon): a Dimension silently drops the opener's reservation (gotcha design-lineheight-multiple)
plate IV's type has an empty numberingTemplate, so a bare :ref would print 'lámina' (or 'plate') and a no-break space; the citation gives its own words with :ref's text

page 6 is the last page of text before the night plate, where 1.4.1 lifts a float below the text to one float gap under it (build.ts hugClosingText) and placement.position 'bottom' changes nothing; plate IV is set there on purpose, one line under the paragraph, and each text is fitted to one page so the plate and its caption end above the folio
bodyText.maxRuntTracking is 0: a runt fix's negative tracking is measured but never painted (gotcha runt-tracking-unpainted)
locale is 'es' or 'en-us', the exact codes: any other tag falls back to American English patterns (gotcha hyphenation-locales)

what.en: The three texts, the captions and the colophon, in Spanish and English, and the six plates, drawn in code
what.es: Los tres textos, los pies y el colofón, en español y en inglés, y las seis láminas, dibujadas en código
